overview: The commission found 36 Mystic Street significant, initiating a public hearing process, and accepted demolition applications for 17 Sharon and 85 Marshall Streets with conditions. The chair also provided major updates regarding the exhumation of the former Cross Street Cemetery and ongoing archaeological surveys.

items.title: 36 Mystic Street Determination of Significance
items.summary: Determined the property is significant due to its Italianate architecture and historical integrity, moving the project to a public hearing. The owner clarified that proposed work is primarily interior renovation and exterior maintenance.

items.title: 17 Sharon Street Demolition Application
items.summary: Accepted the demolition application contingent on the applicant providing graphic elevations and sketches showing the scope of change. The commission will hire a consultant to complete a historical inventory form for the property.

items.title: 85 Marshall Street Demolition Application
items.summary: Accepted the demolition application with conditions requiring additional architectural drawings for proposed alterations. The commission will proceed with a determination of significance next month.

items.title: Medford Square Zoning Discussion
items.summary: Discussed an upcoming joint meeting on Medford Square zoning, with members emphasizing the need for historic building protections and potential design guidelines within the plan.

items.title: Commission Membership and Appointments
items.summary: Provided updates on the appointment process for two new commissioners and invited further public interest for remaining vacancies.

items.title: 41 Mystic Street Preservation
items.summary: Discussed establishing a local historic district to preserve the 18th-century structure due to its historical ties to slavery and the Hall family. The chair noted the potential for relocating the building to a city-owned lot to prevent demolition.

items.title: Brooks Estate and Thomas Brooks Park Archaeological Surveys
items.summary: Reported that the Brooks Estate survey is out to bid and that lab work for artifact cleaning at Thomas Brooks Park is moving into its next phase. Recent excavations at Thomas Brooks Park identified an 18th-century trash midden with artifacts correlating to the site's history of enslaved people.

items.title: Cross Street Cemetery Restoration and Exhumation
items.summary: Announced that the project to remove the City Hall parking lot for the exhumation of remains from the former Cross Street Cemetery is going out to bid. The commission is also seeking funding to restore 85 headstones at the current cemetery site.

items.title: Hastings Heights and Brooks Estate Neighborhood Surveys
items.summary: Confirmed that the Hastings Heights survey has commenced and outlined plans to apply for grants to survey the Brooks Estate neighborhood in 2027.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: Approved meeting minutes and adjourned the meeting.
